title: Redwood Console - tracing + request logs debugging walkthrough
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing and request-logs debugging. SE demoed error-analysis view, trace linkages to request logs, and how to pivot from an error trace to full request payload and KV cache status. Customer asked about noise/sampling, retention, SSO/audit logs, and private deployment (VPC). Agreed next steps: send SOC2 + security pack, pricing for Dedicated pilot, schedule benchmark run, demo to infra team next week.
next_steps: Jonas to send SOC2 and security docs (by 2026-11-02)
Samira to schedule PoC benchmark with Marco (propose dates)
Schedule infra deep-dive with Priya and infra team (next week)
Share sample tracing dashboard and sample request payloads
action_items: Samira: run initial benchmark plan and propose slots to Marco (due 2026-11-04)
Marco: provide sample failing request IDs and retention needs (due 2026-11-03)
transcript:
Header: 2026-10-26 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jonas (Redwood), Samira (Redwood), Priya (Acme CTO), Marco (Acme Platform), Lena (Acme SecOps)

[00:00:00] Jonas: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Jonas, i'm the AE on this account. with me is Samira, our solutions engineer.
[00:00:10] Priya: Hi, thanks. we're excited to see the console flows. we've been seeing a few errors surface in prod and want to understand root cause faster.
[00:00:20] Samira: Great, i'll share my screen — i'm going to walk through the tracing view, then we'll pivot to request logs and show how you can jump from a trace to the full request payload. there might be some small lag while i load the demo data.
[00:00:45] Marco: quick qual — are you demoing hosted or dedicated? we're leaning toward dedicated but want the debug/observability parity.
[00:00:55] Jonas: for this walkthrough i'll show hosted console UI, but almost everything maps to dedicated/private; we have the same tracing and request-log plumbing in Redwood Dedicated or Private V P C installs.
[00:01:10] Samira: ok loading trace map... so on the left is the trace topology, you can see per-span latency and error tags, we surface top error reasons and a heatmap of token-level failures. note: sometimes the auto-summarizer will mislabel an error reason (transcription issue), so always open raw logs.
[00:01:40] Lena: how do you handle sampling? we don't want too much noise, but need retention for audits.
[00:01:50] Samira: good Q. retention and sampling are configurable per-tenant. by default we do adaptive sampling: high-error rate traces are kept at 100%, low-error requests sampled down. you can also configure a policy to keep all requests for specific routes. audit logs are separate and can be forwarded to your SIEM or S3 via our export connectors.
[00:02:20] Priya: and encryption — keys? we use KMS/HSM, need to ensure request bodies aren't stored unencrypted.
[00:02:30] Jonas: we support customer-managed keys — K M S integrs — and at-rest encryption. we can also enable redaction for PII in request logs before storage. we'll share the security pack after.
[00:02:45] Samira: back to the demo, clicking into a failing request — note the trace shows a latency spike at model decode -> kv cache miss. sometimes the ui will show "K V cache" as two words in the transcript export, sorry for that, that's a quirk in the demo dataset.
[00:03:10] Marco: can we see the full request payload and response tokens? we need the ability to repro with the exact prompt and model version.
[00:03:20] Samira: yes — click "open request" and we show headers, full prompt, model version, pins, quantization profile, and the token-level response. you can copy the exact payload to run locally or send to our PoC harness.
[00:03:45] [screen noise/hard-to-hear]
[00:04:10] Priya: what about redaction? we can't send full user messages to third parties.
[00:04:20] Samira: we have field-level redaction rules (regex) and a transform pipeline that'll redact PII before it's persisted or forwarded. it's configurable via console or API.
[00:04:40] Jonas: we also log anonymized traces for product analytics if you enable that — but the default keeps request bodies only in your tenant and encrypted.
[00:05:05] Samira: now i'll show error analysis — here we group similar failures (e.g., truncated responses, hallucination alerts, model OOM). click a group and you get representative traces and a ranked list of contributing factors like batch size, context length, and quantization settings.
[00:05:30] Marco: the OOMs we've seen are sporadic and seem to correlate with long context and a particular quantization profile. can we set an auto-fallback?
[00:05:42] Samira: yes, routing policies support automatic fallback to a larger instance or a less-quantized model variant when we detect repeated OOMs. you can configure thresholds and cooldown windows.
[00:06:05] Lena: for compliance we need immutable audit logs with S S O user attribution. do you write an audit trail?
[00:06:12] Jonas: yes, SAML/SSO is supported and we surface audit logs with user IDs and action types. logs can be pushed to your syslog/Splunk.
[00:06:30] Samira: switching to request-log search — you can filter by request id, model, route, time, or error code. here's a boolean builder for complex filters. There's also a saved-search feature for recurring investigations.
[00:06:55] Priya: the UI looks good. is there an API to query request logs programmatically? we'd like to integrate into our internal incident runbooks.
[00:07:05] Samira: yes, all Console queries are backed by the Request Logs API; you can fetch raw events, traces, and export results. Rate limits apply by plan.
[00:07:20] Marco: about volume — we do ~1.2m requests/day. what's the cost impact of logging everything?
[00:07:28] Jonas: good point. request logging is metered. we recommend sampling or route-level retention to control costs; Redwood Optimize can recommend sampling and batching configs to keep unit costs down while preserving investigatability.
[00:07:50] Samira: demoing a pivot: i click an error trace, then "show similar" which surfaces other requests with same error fingerprint and groups by model-version. you can then bulk-export those request IDs for offline analysis.
[00:08:15] [00:08:15] Samira: i'll intentionally trigger a simulated failing request (demo mode) — you should see the trace appear in the "live" panel within seconds.
[00:08:40] Marco: oh i see it, latency pattern matches. can we attach a reproduction job or a canary?
[00:08:50] Samira: yes, there's an option to create a replay job that will re-run a request against a target model/infra with the same payload and headers for reproducibility. this runs in an isolated job so it doesn't affect production traffic.
[00:09:15] Priya: how are secrets/keys handled in replays? we can't leak customer K M S keys to replayers.
[00:09:25] Samira: replay jobs scrub secrets and can be configured to use ephemeral keys or your own key material in private deployments. we document that in the security pack.
[00:09:40] Jonas: quick interruption — i want to show the tracing timeline view which has a correlation id you can copy to paste into your ticketing system. that way engineers can jump straight from PagerDuty -> trace -> request.
[00:09:58] Lena: do you integrate with PD/SLACK/Teams? we want alerts and links in our channels.
[00:10:05] Jonas: yes integrations for PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Slack; webhook-based alerts too. you can include contextual links to traces and saved searches.
[00:10:25] Samira: showing the error analysis panel now — it surfaces a ranked list of top contributors, and you can run an impact analysis which estimates affected request volume and cost. this helps prioritize fixes.
[00:10:50] Marco: curious about KV cache metrics — you mentioned a cache miss earlier — can we see per-key hit rates?
[00:11:00] Samira: we expose cache hit/miss timeseries and per-route hit rates. if there's a hot-key you'll see it in the metrics and can set up alerts.
[00:11:20] Priya: what about private deployment differences? we're considering a V P C private install due to PHI. will tracing work the same?
[00:11:30] Samira: yes feature parity is the goal. in Private we ship a control plane and you manage the data plane; we provide telemetry collectors that run inside your VPC and forward only metadata unless you opt into forwarding payloads. audit and key management are customer controlled.
[00:11:55] Priya: what's the onboarding timeline for private?
[00:12:02] Jonas: usually 6-8 weeks for initial private deploy assuming infra prep; Dedicated is quicker (2-4 weeks). We'll scope exact times in the PoC scoping doc.
[00:12:20] Marco: can we run a benchmark with our production-like traces?
[00:12:25] Samira: absolutely, that's one of the PoC steps — send sample traces and we'll run them in benchmark mode, show latency distributions, and quantify cost with different batching/quant configs.
[00:12:45] [quiet typing]
[00:13:10] Samira: also demoing the request timeline: click any token and it highlights the corresponding kernel execution time and memory pressure, which helps to identify if a particular token expands computation. 
[00:13:35] Marco: we've had tokenization differences between models cause issues — can you show model comparators?
[00:13:42] Samira: yes, there's a model-compare feature that shows output diffs across model versions and quantization profiles. we show token alignment and delta metrics like hallucination score.
[00:14:05] Priya: talk about access control — RBAC for different teams? we need devs to see traces but not PII.
[00:14:12] Jonas: RBAC supports route-level and field-level permissions; you can restrict who can view raw payloads versus redacted views.
[00:14:30] Samira: demoing saved policies — create a policy that hides request text for Security Analysts or gives read-only metrics access.
[00:14:50] Marco: any offline retention/export formats? we want to keep 7 years for audit.
[00:14:58] Samira: we can export to S3/BigQuery with lifecycle rules; for long-term retention we'll recommend a cold storage export. keep in mind egress costs.
[00:15:20] Priya: what's the SLA for tracing ingestion and console UI?
[00:15:28] Jonas: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed ingestion and 99.9% console uptime — we'll include exact numbers in the contract. hosted customers see high availability but SLA tiers vary.
[00:15:45] Samira: demoing a deeper error — this trace shows model choking due to length; the error analysis suggests truncation or windowed batching as mitigations. you can set automatic pre-flight prompt shortening.
[00:16:10] Marco: has the system flagged any regressions historically? can we tie to model rollouts?
[00:16:20] Samira: yes, rollouts are integrated — when a model rollout increases error rate the console will surface a regression alert and link to the failing traces. you can auto-roll back if thresholds are breached.
[00:16:40] Priya: we heard about Redwood Optimize previously — can it auto-suggest batch sizes and quant profiles based on our traces?
[00:16:48] Jonas: that's exactly the use case — Optimize analyzes your workload and suggests batching, caching, and quantization settings to hit latency and cost targets. it also simulates cost impact.
[00:17:05] [unrelated chatter - background noise]
[00:17:35] Samira: demoing the request log API quickly — here is a curl that fetches events for a request ID, note the token costs returned in headers so you can attribute cost to specific investigations.
[00:17:55] Marco: how granular are cost attributions? per-token? per-route?
[00:18:00] Samira: per-token and per-route breakdowns are available; we also show aggregated cost by model-version and time window.
[00:18:20] Lena: any red flags about HIPAA/PHI — we've got constrained rules in our infra.
[00:18:30] Jonas: Redwood Private is the recommended path for PHI; we support BAA discussions and can provide architecture guidance for isolated data planes.
[00:18:50] Samira: clicking to show an example ticket workflow — engineer clicks "create incident" from the trace and it populates a template with request id, stack trace, model version, and a link to the replay job.
[00:19:10] Marco: very helpful. about performance — what's the typical ingestion to console latency? near-real-time?
[00:19:18] Samira: ingestion-to-UI is usually under 3s for hosted; depends on sampling and export rates. Private can be tuned for lower latency.
[00:19:38] Priya: curious about costs for exporting full request bodies — can we compress or forward only metadata?
[00:19:45] Samira: yes, compression and metadata-only forwarding are supported. we recommend metadata for high-volume routes.
[00:20:05] Jonas: we're nearing the Q/A, any blockers from your side for a PoC?
[00:20:10] Marco: timeline and security sign-offs are the main ones. we'd need SOC2 and architecture review.
[00:20:18] Jonas: we'll send SOC2 + security pack and schedule a dedicated architecture session with our solutions architect.
[00:20:30] Samira: last demo piece — when you click an error group you can run a "what-if" analysis which will show estimated reduction in error volume if you change batching or model. this uses historical traces for sims.
[00:20:55] Priya: that could help us prioritize. Marco, can you pull together a short list of top failing routes?
[00:21:02] Marco: yes i'll do that.
[00:21:10] [long pause — typing]
[00:21:45] Samira: quick note — some names in the transcript export are fuzzy; you'll see "K V cache" or "V P C" sometimes, that's just the speech->text artifact in our demo data. actual console shows proper names.
[00:22:05] Jonas: ok let's recap next steps: Jonas send SOC2 + security pack, Samira schedule PoC benchmark and infra deep-dive, Marco send sample failing request IDs and retention needs.
[00:22:20] Priya: sounds good. can we lock a time for next week Thurs or Fri?
[00:22:28] Samira: i'll follow up with a Doodle and propose Thurs 10am or Fri 2pm.
[00:22:35] Lena: please include our SecOps Slack channel for the architecture session.
[00:22:42] Jonas: will do. any last Qs?
[00:22:48] Marco: one small one — are there built-in safeguards to avoid replays accidentally charging customers?
[00:22:55] Samira: replays are isolated and default to a simulation mode that doesn't bill; for full-run you have to opt-in and provide billing approval.
[00:23:10] Priya: ok great, thanks everyone.
[00:23:15] Jonas: thanks, we'll send the docs. bye.

Footer: Links shared in chat: Security pack (link), sample tracing dashboard (link), PoC scoping doc (link). Note: transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker attribution artifacts.
